images.title: The magic number 142857
images.purpose: Show that 142857 times 1 to 6 gives the same six digits in the same circular order, and 142857 × 7 = 999999.
images.composition: A digit ring on the left and a short column of products on the right; white space between and around them.
exact_structure: Left: 6 digits placed evenly on a teal #0072B2 circle, clockwise from the top: 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7.
Right, above the product column: the heading 142857 in teal #0072B2, so each line below reads as 142857 times that number.
In each of the first 6 lines the first digit of the product is amber #E69F00.
The 7th line, × 7 = 999999, is in reddish purple #CC79A7, set slightly apart below the others.
rejection: the ring digits in any clockwise order other than 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7
more or fewer than 7 product lines
images.takeaway: Multiplying 142857 by 1 to 6 just rotates its digits round the ring, and × 7 gives 999999.
images.description: A ring of the digits 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 beside the products of 142857 with 1 to 7, ending in 999999.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on the cyclic number 142857.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to find the starting digit of each product on the ring and read clockwise.

image_decisions.why: The ring makes the digit rotation visible in a way a list alone cannot.
